top_band: blue-grey tiled roof slope and stone basin rim with water surface (rows 1-16 for roof, rows 30-35 for basin top)
evidence: The structure clearly shows both a deep sloped tiled roof from above (rows 1-16) overhanging two wooden pillars (rows 18-43) with an eave shadow (row 17), and a rectangular stone basin below whose horizontal top rim and recessed water surface are visible from above (rows 30-35) above its vertical front face (rows 36-42).

style.evidence: While the roof has decent tile shading, the lower half is extremely flat and geometric compared to the Beodeul well reference: the wooden posts are 2-colour vertical stripes with no wood grain, the stone basin front is a large 6x12 single-colour flat grey rectangle, the water is a simple 2-tone block, and heavy near-black outlines enclose the shapes.
